$comment: Global tuning surface. Everything the engine reads at runtime lives here; no engine edit should ever be needed to rebalance the game. Times are in LOGIC FRAMES at 60Hz unless the key says 'Seconds'. Distances are world units (a fighter is ~1.8 tall).

timestep.$comment: Logic runs at a fixed 60Hz. maxCatchUpSteps caps how many logic steps one render frame may consume, so a tab that was backgrounded resumes instead of spiral-of-deathing.

stage.$comment: Fighters are clamped to +/- halfWidth. Hitting the wall is what makes corner pressure real.

physics.$comment: pushApart keeps two bodies from occupying the same space; each fighter is displaced half the overlap, and the corner clamp then wins so you can be pinned.

hitstop.$comment: Freeze both fighters for min..max frames, lerped by damage. A jab barely stutters; a special slams. damageAtMax is pinned to the hardest hit in the roster (Titan's 18) so the biggest move actually reaches maxFrames — set it above that and nothing ever earns the full freeze. Current spread: jab 2, punch 3, kick 3-4, special 5-6.

shake.$comment: Only hits at or above heavyDamageThreshold shake the camera, so jabs stay readable. 9 puts both kicks (9 and 12) above the line and both jabs (5 and 7) below it — move it with the roster's damage numbers, not independently.

input.$comment: Attacks fire on the press, not while held. A press opens a buffer this many frames wide, consumed when the move actually starts — so an attack pressed slightly before recovery ends still comes out. Set to 0 for strict frame-perfect input.

camera.$comment: Tracks the midpoint of both fighters. baseDistance already frames a gap of comfortSeparation; only separation BEYOND that pulls the camera back. Without that subtraction the starting gap alone blows the distance out and the fighters render tiny.

ai.$comment: This whole block is the difficulty dial. reactionFrames is how long the AI takes to notice a startup before it can react-block, so lower is harder (below ~5 it blocks even jabs). attackChance is how often it commits when in range, and decisionIntervalFrames how often it re-decides — raise either to make it less relentless. guardReadChance is the high/low mixup dial: at 1 the AI always guards the correct height and low attacks become pointless, at 0 it always guesses wrong; 0.5 is a genuine coin flip. lowAttackChance is how often it goes low itself.

phaseLerp.$comment: The feel of the whole game lives in these four numbers. strike snaps onto the pose on active frames; recovery settles slowly out of it. See also strikeLead below, which decides HOW EARLY in the active window the strike pose is reached.

animation.$comment: useClips=false forces the procedural poser even when retargeted clips loaded — handy for A/B-ing feel.
